text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Luxembourgh Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker announces at joint press conference Luxembourg will contribute U.S.$1 million over three years to Asia-Europe Foundation.
- U.S. government top Asia official Winston Lord is on unannounced visit to China for talks including human rights and alleged Chinese nuclear sales.
- None of 40 foreign companies listed on Stock Exchange of Singapore meets criteria to convert foreign-currency floats into Singapore-dollar listings.
- Singapore retail market recovery unlikely before 2000.
- Economic Development Board expects disk drive sector to achieve double-digit growth this year.
- Newly launched Business Times Singapore Regional Index continues its gains on second day.
- Suppliers to disk drive industry are seeing 5 to 50 percent rise in orders, following months of declines.
- Foreign bankers may get to manage Taiwan's U.S.$86.4 billion forex reserves under liberalisation plans.
- Air fares from Singapore to Britain, U.S. and Australia are down by up to 40 percent.
- Joint-venture of Lum Chang Holdings and Singapore Pools buys Praradiz Centre for Singapore $145 million.
- Hotel Properties Ltd says it has agreed to acquire Four Seasons Hotel in Milan for U.S. $43 million.
- Listed motor and property group Sime Singapore sells BMW business in Brunei to QAF Brunei Sdn Bhd for between Singapore $1 million and $1.5 million.
- Hong Leong Group and CDL Hotels International Ltd eyeing HK $3 billion hotel development.
- Shipping firm Labroy Marine 11 percent oversubscribed in initial public offer of 36.4 million shares to public at Singapore 69 cents.
